title: Doctor: GPU row that says when voice and chat run on CPU
body:
Part of #625 (non-NVIDIA support). Builds on #1056.

Doctor doesn't say anything about the GPU today, so on an AMD/Intel machine (or an NVIDIA one with a broken driver) there's no hint why everything is slow. I want a GPU row in `node-bot/doctor.js` based on `detectGpu()`:
- NVIDIA with CUDA: pass, name + VRAM.
- Anything else: warn, e.g. "No NVIDIA GPU: voice and chat run on CPU.", naming the card that was found (and whether it's integrated/shared memory), or pointing at the driver when an NVIDIA card is there but `nvidia-smi` doesn't answer.
interface: `runDoctorChecks({ ..., gpu })` takes `detectGpu()`'s result (or null) as `gpu` and adds a check with id `"gpu"`. Messages: CUDA card: `"<name> (<GB, 1 decimal> GB VRAM): CUDA available"`; null: exactly `"No NVIDIA GPU: voice and chat run on CPU."`; another card: `"... found <name>, <GB> GB VRAM ... run on CPU"` (with `integrated, shared memory` for a shared-memory GPU); an NVIDIA card without CUDA mentions `nvidia-smi isn't answering`.
why: A new Doctor row built on an existing helper (detectGpu). Tests reusing what is there and matching the surrounding check format.
